blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — VTE prophylaxis after total knee arthroplasty
stem: After total knee replacement, a client is prescribed an anticoagulant as part of the postoperative venous thromboembolism prevention plan. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: The anticoagulant lowers postoperative VTE risk as one part of an individualized prevention plan that also includes appropriate early mobilization, mechanical prophylaxis, and continued assessment.
options.B: The anticoagulant is mainly prescribed to accelerate surgical-wound healing because total knee replacement carries little clinically important risk of DVT or pulmonary embolism.
options.C: Once chemoprophylaxis is prescribed, mobility, compression measures, and observation for thromboembolic symptoms are no longer relevant to postoperative prevention.
options.D: Every joint-replacement client requires the same anticoagulant regimen because VTE prophylaxis should not vary with clotting history, bleeding risk, or postoperative mobility.

rationale: Current AAOS discussion identifies VTE as an important complication after total hip and knee arthroplasty and emphasizes that chemoprophylaxis should be risk-stratified rather than one-size-fits-all. AAOS also describes comprehensive prevention strategies that pair pharmacologic prophylaxis with early mobilization and mechanical measures. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Explain anticoagulant prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty as one component of an individualized VTE-prevention plan that includes mobility, mechanical measures, and ongoing assessment.
source_document_title: Aspirin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after hip and knee arthroplasty is not one-size-fits-all; AAOS VTE prophylaxis resources
source_version_date: AAOS Now article published April 25, 2026; AAOS resources current and accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: AAOS Now 2026: VTE remains an important complication after THA/TKA; prophylaxis must be individualized; comprehensive strategy includes patient assessment, early mobilization, and mechanical prophylaxis. AAOS VTE guidance supports pharmacologic and/or mechanical prophylaxis after elective hip/knee arthroplasty.
source_claim_supported: Post-arthroplasty chemoprophylaxis reduces VTE risk but should be individualized and combined with mobility/mechanical prevention rather than used as a universal stand-alone regimen.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: administer medications safely, educate clients, and evaluate medication response/adverse effects.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all options as complete prophylaxis explanations of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current AAOS risk-stratified VTE-prevention guidance; no second answer or residual length cue remains.
